body:
Supermarkets should be required by law to show the carbon dioxide produced in making each product on its label.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Paths, signposts and wooden walkways should not be built in wild places such as mountains and moorland, even if walkers then cause more damage to the land.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Governments should spend more public money on protecting insects, such as bees and moths, than on protecting large wild mammals such as deer and foxes.

Do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Replacing an old washing machine or fridge with a new energy-efficient model is usually better for the environment than repairing the old one.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people believe that wind farms are the best way to produce clean electricity and should be built in the countryside wherever the wind is strong. Others argue that they spoil the views and harm birds and bats.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some governments think the quickest way to reduce carbon in the air is to plant millions of new trees. Others believe they should protect the ancient forests that already exist.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

In some cities, households that use the most water pay a higher price for each litre. Others argue that everyone should pay the same rate, since clean water is a basic need.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some experts argue that unprofitable farmland should be left to return to wild woodland and marsh through rewilding. Others claim that such land should stay in productive use to feed people and support rural jobs.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many towns now use far more artificial light at night than they need, and the stars are hidden from view.

What problems does this cause?

What can be done to reduce it?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Flooding along rivers has become more frequent in many regions, damaging homes, farmland and roads almost every year.

What are the main causes of this problem?

What measures could be taken to reduce the risk to people and property?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many older houses lose large amounts of heat through their walls and roofs, so families spend heavily on energy and produce unnecessary emissions.

What are the main reasons why so many older homes lack proper insulation?

How can governments encourage homeowners to improve their insulation?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many people now choose to spend their holidays in their own country rather than flying to a distant destination.

Do the advantages of holidaying close to home outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some cities are considering a ban on selling bottled water in public places, arguing that tap water is safe to drink.

Do the advantages of banning bottled water in public places outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some schools teach environmental science mainly outdoors, in woods, rivers and fields, rather than in classrooms.

Do you think the advantages of teaching environmental science outdoors outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Metals such as lithium and cobalt, which are needed for phones and laptops, are often mined in ways that damage landscapes and water supplies.

Why is it so difficult to reduce the environmental cost of mining these metals?

Who should be responsible for ensuring that they are extracted responsibly?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

In many desert regions, communities that have farmed the same land for centuries now face longer droughts and less rainfall than before.

What problems do these changes cause for such communities?

How can people in dry areas adapt their way of life to survive with less water?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many governments are installing smart meters in homes so that households can see how much electricity they use at each hour of the day.

Why might some households be reluctant to accept these meters?

What could energy companies do to encourage people to use them more wisely?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
